coverage: Three canvases from one scan set: Great Lakes basin (config/great_lakes_bounds.json, lon -93..-73.5, lat 40.5..49.5, 1800x1175), North American continental (config/north_america_bounds.json, lon -180..-15, lat 5..85, 3300x1600), worldwide global (config/global_bounds.json, lon -180..180, lat -90..90, 3600x1800). Full rectangles; valid pixels paint everywhere observed (oceans included); missing stays transparent, never 0%.
display_units: IR brightness (white = cold cloud tops; not a percentage)
fallback_note: No model fill. VIIRS I5 Day/Night (daily, via NASA GIBS) supplements ONLY pixels with no valid geostationary observation (poles, seams); documented as daily in metadata.
freshness_label: LIVE / CURRENT IR OBSERVATION (multi-satellite, honest timestamps)
mosaic_policy: Geostationary preferred over VIIRS-daily. Fresher GEO scan wins overlaps; skew within 15 min gets a 12-px cross-fade, larger skews resolve hard to the fresher observation. Coldest-wins never used. Antimeridian blended. Provenance recorded per pixel (see provenance.png).
precedence: 1) GOES-19 + GOES-18 ABI L2 CMIPF Band-13 direct BT. 2) Himawari-9 Band-13 via GIBS WMTS with documented LUT inversion (+/-0.5C). 3) Meteosat FES (0 deg) + IODC (45.5E) SEVIRI IR10.8 via EUMETView WMS grayscale imagery (imagery-derived transfer). 4) VIIRS I5 daily only where no GEO valid. Missing observations stay transparent.
sat_note: GOES FD 10-min; Himawari 10-min; Meteosat 15-min; VIIRS daily. Geostationary limbs degrade toward disk edges (documented limitation); polar regions depend on the daily VIIRS supplement and may show swath-age boundaries.

satellites.meteosat_iodc: Meteosat-9 (45.5E), SEVIRI IR10.8 L1.5 via EUMETView WMS msg_iodc:ir108, 15-min, grayscale imagery transfer

source_name: GOES-19/18 ABI infrared + Himawari-9 infrared (via NASA GIBS) + Meteosat SEVIRI infrared imagery (via EUMETSAT EUMETView) + VIIRS daily polar supplement (via NASA GIBS)
title: LIVE CLOUD COVER
variable: Infrared window brightness (GOES/Himawari BT in K, VIIRS BT in K, Meteosat grayscale imagery) -> white-cloud brightness + transparency. Not a cloud-cover percentage.
